title: Tech Sector Displacement by 2030: Uneven by Experience Level
description: The weighted average (11%) reflects a mix of direct employment measures and job-posting proxy data. One peer-reviewed study (Brynjolfsson et al. 2025) finds net tech employment grew +1.3%, but this masks a K-shaped split: developers aged 22-25 saw ~20% employment decline since late 2022, while those 35-49 grew +9%. Job posting data from Indeed, Lightcast, and BLS show 13-22% declines in tech hiring volume. The primary channel is not mass layoffs but evaporated entry points — firms stopped creating junior roles as senior devs absorb that work with AI tools.

The 13.8% annualized figure reflects this narrow category's decline; sector-wide tech displacement is much lower.

sources.title: Autonomous Coding Agents Generate 400,000+ Pull Requests: Real-World Software Workflow Implications
sources.excerpt: Autonomous coding agents are generating code at an unprecedented scale, with OpenAI Codex alone creating over 400,000 pull requests (PRs) in two months. CRA-only PRs achieve a 45.20% merge rate, 23.17 percentage points lower than human-only PRs (68.37%), with significantly higher abandonment. 60.2% of closed CRA-only PRs fall into the 0-30% signal range.

sources.title: AI and Coder Employment: Compiling the Evidence

Cumulating over the roughly 3 years since November 2022 and using 5.735 million coder jobs as the base value, the implication is that roughly 500,000 additional coder jobs would have existed in the absence of large-scale LLM use.

sources.title: Inside the AI Index: 12 Takeaways from the 2026 Report

The pattern repeats in other jobs with higher levels of AI exposure, like customer service. Meanwhile, firm surveys indicate executives expect this trend to accelerate, with planned headcount reductions outpacing recent cuts.
